title: Trace context enrichment and intelligent pager filtering for low-signal alerts
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Problem: Our current alerting surface generates noisy pages for transient latency spikes and low-signal errors originating from downstream services. Existing burn-rate alerts trigger repeatedly on broad aggregates and lack enough request-level context to correctly attribute root cause, which leads to unnecessary paging and follow-on operational toil.

Goal: Reduce false-positive paging by enriching traces with request-context metadata and introducing a lightweight on-edge noise filter + local anomaly detector that annotates signals prior to SLO burn-rate evaluation. Improvements should: (1) attach stable request path identifiers and feature flags to spans, (2) allow per-route adaptive sampling for tracing and metric aggregation, and (3) add a scoring stage that suppresses pages unless a high-confidence attribution to Redwood runtime or core infra exists.

Scope: Instrument trace hooks in the API gateway and runtime ingress to attach contextual attributes (customer_id, route_signature, model_variant, auth_tier) and a short-lived request fingerprint. Implement a stream enrichment stage in the telemetry pipeline that writes enriched spans to the trace-store and emits augmented metric tags used by SLO evaluation. Build a simple on-host anomaly filter using EWMA + change-point detector for latency distributions and expose a confidence score to the burn-rate engine. Update paging policy configuration to incorporate confidence score and route ownership heuristics.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Trace hooks deployed to gateway and runtime ingress capturing request context for 95% of requests in staging.
2) Telemetry pipeline enrichment upstream of the SLO engine that adds route_signature and model_variant tags to latency/error metrics.
3) Local anomaly filter prototype running as a sidecar on dedicated pods producing a confidence score (0.0-1.0) persisted alongside metrics.
4) Burn-rate alerting rules extended to require confidence >= 0.65 for automatic paging; lower-confidence alerts only create tickets/notifications in Slack channel #infra-alerts.
5) Pager volume reduced by >= 30% in the first 7 days of rollout on the canary tenant without missing any P0 incidents in that window.
6) Runbook updated with the new attribution fields and playbook for manually escalating suppressed alerts.
implementation_notes:
Architecture decisions and trade-offs considered: we evaluated moving confidence computation entirely into the central pipeline but chose a small on-host filter to keep high-signal decisions close to telemetry origin and to reduce ingestion cost. The sidecar uses a two-tier approach: an EWMA baseline for latency shifts and a lightweight Bayesian change-point detector for abrupt jumps.

Data model: add 'route_signature' (string), 'request_fp' (short hash), 'model_variant' (string), 'auth_tier' (string), and 'anomaly_confidence' (float stringified) as tags on metrics and span attributes. We will backfill only for traces retained for later debugging; metrics will default to 'unknown' tag if unavailable to avoid dropping series.

Ops considerations: config flags for per-tenant sampling rate and confidence threshold live in config-store under /observability/pager/thresholds. Default confidence for paging is 0.65, adjustable per-customer. Logging level for the sidecar must be rate-limited; use token-bucket at 10/s.

Compatibility: no changes to public SDKs. Ensure the enrichment stage respects PII redaction rules; customer_id must be hashed with HMAC using platform KMS key prior to being sent to the telemetry plane.
